cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, gets a message from the LORD for the Israelites about a special vow: the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD. Friend, this is not a casual promise. This is a COMMITMENT.

cards.question: Who can make the special vow of a Nazirite?

cards.text: Rule number one is about the grapevine: a Nazirite is to abstain from wine and strong drink, and even from vinegar made from them. Vinegar, friend? Who's out here SIPPING vinegar?

cards.question: Grape juice and raisins are still fine for a Nazirite, since there's no wine in them.

cards.text: "All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins." That's like swearing off cookies and then finding out the CRUMBS count too.
Rule number two is about his head. For the entire period of the vow, there's one thing that must never touch it.

cards.question: For the entire period of the vow, no ___ shall touch the Nazirite's head.

cards.text: So his hair grows long, and he must be holy until his time of separation to the LORD is complete. Friend, a guy who uses his mustache as HANDS is not about to say one word about this rule.
Rule number three: throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.

cards.question: If the Nazirite's own father or mother dies during the vow, he may go near the body just this once.
Why must a Nazirite stay away from a dead body, even a family member's?

answers.text: His head carries the sign of his vow to God
His hands carry the offerings for the altar
His robe carries the mark of his tribe

cards.text: Throughout his separation, he is holy to the LORD. But if someone suddenly dies in his presence, that defiles his consecrated head of hair.

cards.question: When a sudden death defiles a Nazirite's hair, what must he do on his day of cleansing?
The Nazirite's day of cleansing comes on the ___ day.

cards.text: On the eighth day, he brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make atonement for him.

cards.question: On the eighth day, after the offerings, the Nazirite has to consecrate his head all over again.

cards.text: Then he must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. And now the question I'd be SWEATING over: what about all the days he already put in?

cards.question: What happens to the days of the vow a Nazirite already kept before he was defiled?

answers.text: They count toward the new vow

cards.text: Now the happy part, friend: the FINISH LINE. When the Nazirite's time of separation is complete, he's brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

Then come the offerings, and they just KEEP coming: an unblemished male lamb, female lamb and ram, with grain and drink offerings and a basket of unleavened cakes and wafers. The priest presents it all before the LORD and offers the ram as a peace offering.

cards.question: Right at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite shaves his consecrated head and puts the hair on the ___ under the peace offering.

cards.text: The priest puts the ram's boiled shoulder, one unleavened cake and one unleavened wafer into the Nazirite's hands. Then the priest waves them as a wave offering before the LORD.

cards.question: Once the ram's shoulder, the cake and the wafer are waved before the LORD, who are they a holy portion for?
After the shave and the wave offering, the Nazirite may drink wine.

cards.text: Then the LORD sums it up: this is the law of the Nazirite, and his offering comes in addition to whatever else he can afford. As a stamper who once sold for 25 cents, I appreciate that line.

cards.question: Whatever vow a Nazirite makes, what must he do with it?
